title: Runtime: export queue depth + scheduler lag metrics for overload protection (low-cardinality)
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
We need a small set of runtime-exported capacity signals that can be used by routing/admission control to trigger tier-aware overload protection (gate best-effort first, preserve enterprise budgets). The signals must be stable, cheap to compute, and safe from high-cardinality blowups.

This ticket implements runtime instrumentation + export for:
- Queue depth (per model pool and optionally per route group)
- Scheduler lag (time-in-queue / dispatch delay)
- Optional supporting signals to validate correctness (active requests, batch size, kv cache pressure) while keeping tag set bounded

Constraints:
- Must not add meaningful overhead to the hot path (avoid per-request tagging work)
- Cardinality must be explicitly bounded (no tenant_id/customer_id, no raw route, no prompt length buckets at high resolution)
- Must support per-route aggregation via a small route_group / endpoint_group dimension derived upstream (gateway/routing) rather than raw path

Why: Without these signals, routing can’t reliably detect saturation early enough, leading to tail-latency cascades and 5xx on enterprise routes during bursts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Export queue depth and scheduler lag metrics from runtime process to Prometheus/OTel pipeline with <1% CPU overhead under load test
- Provide a bounded tag set: {region, cluster, pool, model_family, route_group, tier} where tier/route_group are optional and must be low-cardinality enums
- Default aggregation works even when route_group is missing (falls back to "unknown")
- Documented in runtime metrics README and linked from SRE dashboard spec
- Verified in staging + us-east canary: metrics present, non-zero under induced load, and correlate with routing admission-control behavior
- No new high-cardinality labels introduced (validated via metrics backend cardinality report)
- Alert queries in ENG-4926 can be written without per-tenant dimensions
implementation_notes:
Proposed metrics (names aligned with overload event standard draft):
1) redwood_runtime_queue_depth{pool,model_family,route_group,tier,region,cluster}
  - Gauge: number of pending requests waiting for scheduler admission.
  - Sampling: every 1s (configurable), computed from scheduler queue length.

2) redwood_runtime_scheduler_lag_ms_p50/p95{pool,model_family,route_group,tier,region,cluster}
  - Gauge or summary-like export via in-process histogram rolled up to p50/p95 at scrape time.
  - Definition: (time_request_enqueued -> time_dispatched_to_gpu).
  - Implementation detail: record enqueue timestamp in request context already present; avoid per-token instrumentation.

3) redwood_runtime_inflight_requests{pool,model_family,region,cluster}
  - Gauge to help explain spikes and validate queue depth.

Tag cardinality policy:
- route_group is a small enum produced upstream (e.g., chat, embeddings, rerank, other). Do NOT use raw HTTP path.
- tier is also a small enum (enterprise, pro, self_serve, unknown). If not available in runtime context, omit initially.
- model_family is normalized (e.g., llama, mistral, qwen) not full model_id.
- pool is the runtime pool name (bounded by config; do not include per-tenant pools).

Data flow:
- Routing attaches x-redwood-route-group header (or equivalent request metadata) when forwarding to runtime.
- Runtime reads route_group from request metadata and uses it only for aggregated counters/histograms.

Rollout plan:
- Ship behind runtime flag: RUNTIME_EXPORT_OVERLOAD_SIGNALS=1 (default off)
- Enable in staging for 48h + run synthetic load
- Enable canary in us-east for allowlisted protected routes
- Monitor cardinality + scrape size before enabling globally
risk_and_mitigations:
Risks:
- Cardinality regression if route_group or pool proliferates unintentionally.
- Overhead if scheduler lag recording is done per token or in a tight loop.
- Semantics drift across runtime versions causing routing thresholds to be mis-tuned.

Mitigations:
- Hard cap allowed route_group values in runtime; map unknowns to "other"
- Use queue-level timestamps (enqueue/dispatch) only; no per-token timing
- Add unit test that rejects adding labels like tenant_id/model_id/route/raw_path
- Add a CI check / dashboard note to monitor series count for redwood_runtime_* metrics
comments: 2025-10-14 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Creating this for runtime to export queue depth + scheduler lag. Routing needs a deterministic signal for admission control; GPU saturation alone is too noisy/laggy. Please keep label set bounded; no tenant_id.

2025-10-15 — Sofia Ivanova (Runtime scheduling): Queue depth is straightforward (scheduler queue length). Scheduler lag needs a precise definition: enqueue->dispatch, not end-to-end latency. We can expose p50/p95 from a small histogram per pool/route_group; anything more granular will blow up series count.

2025-10-16 — Julian Moore (Assignee): Drafted metric names + tags. Request: routing to pass a stable route_group enum so we don’t rely on HTTP path. Otherwise we’ll export only by pool/model_family initially.

2025-10-17 — Elena Popov (Routing): We can add route_group as forwarded metadata; will be one of {chat, embeddings, rerank, other}. Will land in ENG-4924; for now runtime should accept missing and default to "unknown".

2025-10-22 — Logan Wright (Telemetry): Please avoid exporting per-route_group *and* per-model_id. Use model_family only. Also do not include prompt_length_bucket. If you need distribution, do it in logs/traces not metrics.

2025-10-28 — Julian Moore (Assignee): PR up with queue depth + scheduler lag histogram (rollup to p50/p95) per {pool, model_family, route_group}. Added allowlist mapping for route_group; unknown->other. Flagged off by default.

2025-11-02 — Peter Holtz (Embedded SRE): Tested in staging with synthetic burst. Queue depth and lag correlate with routing throttles in the prototype. p95 lag spikes ~30s before p99 latency goes bad—good early-warning signal.

2025-11-07 — Aisha Bello (SRE): Noticed series count jumped after enabling in staging due to pool label including full pool name with shard suffix. Please normalize pool to configured base name (no per-shard).
2025-11-08 — Julian Moore (Assignee): Fixed pool label normalization (strip shard suffix; cap values). Re-ran staging enablement; series count stable. Marking ready for us-east canary.

2025-11-20 — Rafael Mendes (SRE): Canary validated; metrics now used for admission thresholds in routing + dashboards. Closing. Follow-up: add doc snippet for runtime metric semantics so Support/CS doesn’t misinterpret "lag" as model latency.
resolution: Implemented runtime-exported queue depth and scheduler lag signals behind a feature flag with bounded labels and route_group support. Validated in staging and us-east canary; no sustained cardinality issues after pool label normalization. Metrics are now consumable by routing admission control and SRE dashboards for hot-route overload protection.
next_steps:
1) (Optional) Add tier dimension once runtime receives tier metadata reliably from routing (keep enum bounded).
2) Add a short semantics section to the SRE runbook explaining how to interpret queue depth vs scheduler lag.
3) Monitor series count weekly for the first month post-GA and alert on unexpected growth.
